name: Papa Bois
description: Papa Bois ('Father of the Forest') is the protector spirit of forests and wildlife in Trinidad and Tobago and parts of the wider Lesser Antilles, depicted as an old, hairy, hooved man who guards animals from hunters and punishes those who waste or abuse the forest.
full_description: Papa Bois - also called Papa Bwa, Maitre Bois ('master of the woods') or Daddy Bouchon ('hairy man') - is one of the central figures of Trinidad and Tobago folklore, with closely related traditions in Saint Lucia, Dominica, and Grenada. He is described as an aged but powerfully built man covered in hair, with cloven hooves (most often the left foot) and small horns, and a beard that may be made of leaves. He carries a hollowed-out cow horn that he sounds to warn the animals of an approaching hunter. Papa Bois is the protector of the forest and its creatures: respectful travellers and ethical hunters are granted safe passage, but those who hunt wantonly, kill nursing animals, or destroy the forest are punished - sometimes by being lured deep into the bush in the form of a deer, sometimes by being made to marry his consort, the river-spirit Mama D'Lo. The figure synthesizes West African, French, and Indigenous Amerindian elements characteristic of Trinidad's Creole folklore.
origin: Papa Bois is principally a Trinidadian and Tobagonian folklore figure; closely related figures appear in the French/Creole-influenced islands of the Lesser Antilles, including Saint Lucia, Dominica, and Grenada.

etymology.origin: From French Creole / Caribbean French patois: 'papa' (father) + 'bois' (wood/forest).
etymology.meaning: 'Father of the Wood' / 'Father of the Forest'.
etymology.first_use: Documented in Trinidad and Tobago folklore collections from the late 19th and 20th centuries; the figure circulates orally in Creole-speaking Caribbean communities.

timeline.event: Papa Bois emerges in the syncretic folklore of French-influenced Trinidadian Creole communities
timeline.significance: Formation of Papa Bois as a distinct Creole forest-guardian figure

timeline.event: Papa Bois is established as a stock character in Trinidad and Tobago folklore education and Carnival traditions

related.name: Mama D'Lo
related.description: River-spirit consort of Papa Bois in Trinidadian folklore

related.name: Douen
related.description: Trinidadian forest spirits of unbaptised children, sharing the forest landscape with Papa Bois

related.name: Curupira
related.description: Brazilian Indigenous forest-guardian spirit with reversed feet who punishes hunters

cultural_notes: When meeting Papa Bois, one should greet him respectfully (e.g., 'Bon jour, vieux Papa') and avoid staring at his hooves. Showing respect for the forest and its animals secures his protection; cruelty or waste invites punishment.
